name: Shapley Supercluster
tagline: The Shapley Concentration — the heaviest nearby supercluster, ~650 Mly out, containing ~8,000 galaxies.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Pulls the Local Group alongside the Great Attractor

history: The Shapley Supercluster is the largest nearby mass concentration — a titanic knot of about two dozen rich galaxy clusters first mapped by Harlow Shapley in 1930. Its gravity adds measurably to the tug on the Local Group, pulling us beyond what the Great Attractor alone can explain. It stands as a proof that the supercluster scale is itself a unit of cosmic structure, not just a loose label.
